summary: Ontario's highest point, Ishpatina Ridge, had an 80 ft tower from 1930; its 100 ft successor still stands, abandoned since the 1960s.

access.note: Ridge lies in Lady Evelyn-Smoothwater Provincial Park and is reached by remote canoe, portage or winter routes. No source says the abandoned tower is open to climb.

visit.trail_note: Most popular approach is canoe and portage from Capreol by a logging road to the south; a northern route from Gowganda has many portages.

events.note: First tower on the ridge, 80 ft (24 m), per Firelookout.ca

notes_for_editor: The 1930 build year and the 80 ft and 100 ft heights come from Firelookout.ca, a community index, not an agency record; Wikipedia gives the same 1930 and 80 ft (24 m) figures, so they are backed by two sources. The 1960s abandonment is the same single source and gives only the decade, so no abandoned event is recorded (no year to put on it). Ontario tower layer (data/raw/ontario_lio/fire_towers.geojson, OBJECTID 2888): the Ishpatina point has no height, construction date or detail. A separate entry, OBJECTID 2762, OFFICIAL_NAME 'Pinetorch Fire Tower', shows HEIGHT_ABOVE_GROUND 80, ground elevation 2273 ft, and the comment 'Ishpatina Ridge - highest known point in Ontario', at a point about 28 km away (my estimate from the coordinates). It may be the 1930 tower logged under the wrong name and place. Not used in the story; editor to check. Location: Wikipedia puts the ridge in Ellis Township, Sudbury District, 90 km north of Sudbury; the record gives Greater Sudbury as the local unit, which the story follows. The access level 'public' is inferred from provincial park status and the abandoned tower's lack of any closure notice; no source says the tower is open. Wikipedia describes winter-time ski or snowshoe approaches on the northern route, which the access note covers. Nothing found on who built the tower, the 'Ellis' name's origin, or when staffing ended. No photo with a licence found (the Wikipedia 'Ellis Fire Tower, 2015' image was not checked for licence). Fact-check 2026-10-20: story wording on the Maple Mountain comparison was tightened to match the source's 'more popular' phrasing.
